"It is completely reversible and low cost: zero database writes, zero routing changes, and results can be discarded. Keep national rollout on hold pending the query results."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Person: Farah Iqbal, Customer Care Operations, because she owns IVR journey stages, case-creation conditions, and the containment definition."
"What written pass threshold and observation window govern pilot-to-national expansion?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression" overstates what the evidence establishes: the data supports missing case creation, but not that all pre-authentication drops were complaints or that the full ticket decline is attributable to that mechanism.

"The 650 pre-authentication drops ... represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution" treats abandonment as friction and rules out successful resolution without journey linkage, downstream recovery evidence, or sampled call review.

"South network events ... remained steady across May and June" is imprecise because the cited event counts and affected-account estimates changed (10 to 8 events and 9,409 to 7,045 accounts), even if they do not show a comparable improvement.
"low repeat rates support genuine containment" is too strong: low recontact could also reflect unmeasured attrition, delayed contact, or use of other channels.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the important alternative that authenticated users may have received genuine self-service through the new `balance_check` and `pack_info` stages, while also recognizing that pre-authentication abandonment is not equivalent to a CareDesk complaint. It missed a fuller benign interpretation of pre-authentication abandonment—such as successful resolution through another channel or non-complaint IVR exits—and did not propose sampled call listening to distinguish these cases.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add linked journey validation with a targeted sample of pre-authentication abandoned calls, checking whether callers subsequently resolved the issue, repeated contact, reached another channel, or experienced a complaint-worthy failure; this would directly test the claim that abandonment represents suppressed complaints rather than merely querying repeat contacts.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The 4 records occur on 27, 28, 29 May and 4 June; INV-17/03/22/09 each seen once, total duration 13 minutes,” explicitly citing inverter_events.csv rows 1–4 and named fields.
“impact_mw=0 and cleared=yes: 0/4 rows open and 0/4 have nonzero generation loss,” tied to the specified CSV fields.
“The strongest label is one 7-minute COMM_LINK_WARN; other 3 rows are info,” tied to event, severity, and duration_min.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission cross-checks severity, duration, inverter identity, cleared status, and impact rather than relying only on alarm wording.
It considers the innocent/data-quality explanation that the export may be incomplete or filtered and proposes an unfiltered read-only query.
The analysis is principally based on one export and does not independently corroborate the zero-impact field against SCADA or production telemetry.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “Confirm completeness before treating it as representative; this is a data-scope check, not evidence of equipment breakdown” appropriately separates uncertainty from evidence.
The conditional conclusion—reassess if unfiltered records show open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events—identifies decision-changing evidence.

“These observations give zero escalation signal” and “Escalation requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” are somewhat broader and more categorical than the four-row export alone supports.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and make no equipment change” is proportionate to four cleared, zero-impact, short-duration records.
The proposed “read-only export query for the same date range without severity/status filters” is reversible and directly tests the main scope uncertainty.
The stopping rule—stop if the unfiltered query confirms only these four rows, otherwise reassess—is discriminating and operationally appropriate.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Do not escalate on this 4-row extract” accurately scopes the conclusion to the observed extract.
The conclusion recognizes the seven-minute communications warning without treating it as proof of plant failure.
The recommendation preserves a low-priority completeness check while avoiding unsupported equipment intervention.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Routine” is an inference from a small extract, not directly established by the records.
“These observations give zero escalation signal” is too absolute; they provide no observed generation-loss signal, but export incompleteness remains unresolved.
“Escalation requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” is a prescriptive threshold not demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
“Zero recurrence” is valid only within this four-row extract and should not be generalized beyond its scope.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be filtered or incomplete, so the absence of open, recurring, or nonzero-impact events may be an artifact of extraction rather than proof that no plant issue exists. A communications warning could also merit a low-priority data or telemetry-quality check even though this extract shows no MW impact.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed unfiltered export and verify extraction metadata, including the actual date range and any severity/status filters; if available, cross-check the zero-impact field against plant production or SCADA telemetry.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed and reproducible: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%,” tied to `dispatch_blocks.csv` and `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md`.
Observed/model calculation: the submission identifies `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source` for the 12 revised blocks.
Inference is explicitly separated from observation: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”
The commercial-value limitation is traced to `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`, including the Rs 2.72/kWh energy valuation and missing complete net-settlement calculation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly identifies that the headline is a cross-day comparison: “It is a cross-day comparison,” and reports all eight daily penalty totals.
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual by applying the documented penalty to `base_schedule_mw` versus actual generation, estimating Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086 submitted.
It tests plausible innocent explanations and limitations, including baseline weather variation, selection/timing, lack of randomized control, metric definition, and repeatability.
It triangulates penalty totals with block deviations, net daily imbalance, firmware/wind fields, and commercial settlement information rather than treating the 31.6% figure alone as causal proof.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion distinguishes “pilot day performed better” from causation: “causal attribution is rejected” and “17.6% ... [is] a modeled one-day estimate.”
It states what remains unknown: whether the comparator was selected pre-outcome, whether revisions preceded generation, whether effects replicate, and whether net value is positive.
It specifies decision-changing evidence rather than using a generic caveat: immutable timestamps, a pre-registered comparator rule, matched pilot days, and reconciled net commercial data.
It appropriately retains a smaller positive modeled result instead of overcorrecting to no value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“Defer national expansion”—follows from the limited one-day, non-randomized evidence and unresolved net-value question.
The proposed immediate action, “read-only shadow calculation,” preserves operational constraints because it changes “no submitted schedule, plant control, or source record.”
The next test is discriminating: pre-register matched high-wind days, preserve immutable pre-submission timestamps, repeat the shadow calculation, and include net commercial value.
The recommendation reports both quantities with proper scope: “31.6% only as the descriptive 28-to-29 May difference” and “17.6% only as the modeled one-day estimate.”

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the strongest supported interpretation: arithmetic is confirmed, but the 31.6% causal claim is rejected.
It preserves the evidence-supported narrower claim: “On 29 May, replacing 12 `qca_base` blocks with `pilot_revision` reduced modeled deviation penalties by ~17.6% against realized generation.”
It does not claim that the same-day estimate proves causal impact or positive commercial value.
The scope is appropriately limited to one day and 12 revised blocks, consistent with the supplied evidence and rubric.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The within-day modeled counterfactual ... is approximately 17.6% savings” is supported arithmetically, but “savings” could be read as commercial savings; it is correctly narrowed elsewhere to modeled deviation-penalty reduction.
“Read-only shadow calculation ... is cheap and fully reversible” is a reasonable operational characterization, but cost is not quantified in the cited materials.
The submission states that the 28 and 29 May rows have “similar listed wind fields”; this is traceable to the cited file but does not itself establish comparability or causal validity.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May pilot day may genuinely have improved schedule alignment, as suggested by the same-day 17.6% modeled penalty reduction and lower deviation metrics, but the observed difference could still reflect block selection, timing, forecast conditions, or the validity of substituting the base schedule. The evidence supports a favorable association and continued testing, not a 31.6% causal estimate or proven net commercial benefit.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Validate the same-day counterfactual with immutable pre-submission timestamps and a pre-registered rule for selecting revised blocks, then repeat the base-versus-submitted shadow calculation across several matched high-wind days while reconciling penalty, meter, revenue, and pilot-cost data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix confirms 90211000 is valid for Switzerland" is stronger than the submission's own qualification that the matrix "requires Tares confirmation"; the matrix appears to support a reference value, not conclusively establish legally effective classification.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence-of-evidence assertion whose scope is not explicitly defined, although the cited packet sources are identified.

per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the effective Tares or ruling record for P1001 on 2025-11-04, including its jurisdiction, effective date, and product scope, before characterizing the Swiss Matrix entry as legally valid.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place an administrative hold on the Irish preferential tariff claim."
"Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs, and do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is broader than the evidence establishes; the applicable trade rule may permit other forms of origin proof, and the submission itself appropriately identifies the governing rule as still missing.

"EU suppliers SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" overstates what supplier nationality and register currency establish; they would support further investigation, not by themselves prove preferential origin or shipment linkage.

"Valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" is somewhat too categorical because validity, shipment coverage, applicable rule, and product-specific qualification would still need verification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid despite the packet gap: the shipment could have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or a current supplier declaration may exist in offline procurement archives. The evidence therefore supports an administrative documentation hold, not rejection of preference, fraud, or a conclusion based on United States manufacturing country.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the applicable preferential-origin rule and distinguish the legally sufficient evidence it requires from a supplier declaration, then test the sourcing linkage and transaction coverage against that rule before treating any declaration as decision-changing.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "`evidence_available_ts` or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches"
"Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows"
"Follow the 42 HOLD rows to disposition or use survival/right-censoring analysis"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not traceable as stated because the submission also says the required evidence-available timestamp is absent; this appears to conflate a filtered proxy with the SOP KPI.

"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" overstates what coincidence with the snapshot time establishes. It supports a timestamp-semantics or interface-commit concern, but does not by itself prove synchronization caused the values or that actual release decisions occurred at different times.

"their omission biases completed-only cycle-time estimates downward" is directionally plausible given the receipt-date separation, but the claim that the 42 unfinished rows are likely to become the slowest observations is not demonstrated; some may resolve quickly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps may be valid interface commit times rather than simple extract defaults, while still failing to represent the underlying decision time. In that case the apparent long cycle is a mixture of genuine workflow delay and timestamp/interface delay; real queue performance remains unresolved rather than wholly explained by synchronization.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the event-level timestamp definition or audit log that distinguishes required-evidence availability, disposition decision, and QCore interface commit for the same sampled batches, with aligned QCore and CertVault snapshot times. This would directly discriminate a workflow-delay explanation from a measurement-timing explanation; the proposed live sample is useful but matching or differing displayed timestamps alone may not establish decision-time semantics.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot" — cites `source_freshness.csv` and distinguishes stale global availability from current confirmation.

"Revision-B valve supply is two free units ... against four units of revision-B demand" — traces the claim to specific request IDs and rows in `spare_parts.csv`, `part_requests.csv`, and `part_restrictions.csv.
"All four not-transferable requests are MTR-4401 servo-drive requests" — triangulates stock, reservation, and maintenance-email evidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers" and "semantic similarity ... is not transferability" — correctly separates retrieval from operational eligibility.
"Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected using reservation and zero-stock evidence.
The claim that semantic search is not the real problem is plausible for populated MPNs, but the analysis does not yet test semantic-search recall or value on the 11 blank-MPN requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Actionable now still requires current confirmation" — appropriately downgrades certainty because the MaintStar snapshot is old.
"Needs check" and "Not transferable" classifications are tied to revision, quantity, reservation, identity, and freshness conditions.
The phrase "resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" overstates what an exact join establishes, since the subsequent eligibility checks show that retrieval is not resolution.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers" — provides a safe decision rule that protects against reservation, revision, qualification, and stale-stock risks.
The 8/12/4 triage and separate candidate/actionable value framing make the recommendation operationally useful.
"Defend only the eight-request actionable slice ... test search on the 11 blank-MPN requests" — proposes a focused and reversible next step rather than an unconditional technology purchase.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects automatic transfer, family-level interchangeability, interpreting available quantity -1 as zero, and the assumption that an expensive semantic-search system is required.
"The hypothesis survives only if records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check" — preserves a plausible alternative rather than treating the static extract as definitive.
The strongest competing explanation—that semantic search materially improves recall for blank or erroneous MPNs—is acknowledged but not empirically tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records" is a targeted request for the 11 blank-part-number requests.
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query" directly addresses stale and negative-availability records.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search" specifies a discriminating test and explains how its result changes the decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Semantic search is not the real problem" and "master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority" are not fully established because exact MPN matching only addresses populated-MPN requests; the 11 blank-MPN requests remain untested.
"An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" conflates candidate retrieval with transfer resolution, despite later acknowledging eligibility and freshness checks.
The label "actionable now" is somewhat overstated while the relevant global stock snapshot is stale and live CMMS confirmation remains required.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still provide substantial value for the 11 blank-MPN requests or for records with incorrect, incomplete, or nonstandard identifiers. Exact-join success on populated MPNs demonstrates a strong baseline but does not establish that semantic search has low incremental recall or value overall.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small labeled pilot on the 11 blank-MPN requests: obtain maintenance-record identities and revisions, compare exact/manual lookup with semantic-search candidates, then validate candidates against live CMMS availability and restrictions. Measure valid-candidate recall and precision; use the result to decide between data cleanup alone and a semantic-search pilot.
